sections.title: Form and identification
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Bellis perennis, the common daisy, a low perennial forming a basal rosette and spreading by short runners. Flower stalks can reach about 25 cm; the flower heads are usually around 2–3 cm across, with white rays often flushed pink beneath and a yellow disc.

sections.title: Food and image
sections.text: Young leaves are reported eaten as a salad green and the flower heads are also used as food in some references; the flavour is mildly bitter. The plate shows the characteristic rosette, pink-backed white rays, yellow disc and small fruits.
